items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Recover a WRITE producer from a consumer restart
items.author: ChengYM5685
items.summary: Fixes MoRIIO WRITE producer recovery after consumer restart by detecting stale incarnation and dropping peer sessions.
items.body:
## Overview

A MoRIIO WRITE producer never recovers when its consumer restarts alone: it keeps writing over the sessions, QPs and remote memory of the dead process, every transfer fails with `transport retry counter exceeded`, and every request through the pair times out until the producer is restarted too. This gives each launch an incarnation, makes the producer detect the change, drop the stale peer and handshake again, and fail the in-flight transfer at once.

## Claims

- After a decode (consumer) engine restarts, the prefill (producer) engine serves new requests again without being res

items.title: [Fix] mem_cache: Cap device KV slots owned by external-linker prefetch reads
items.author: zijiexia
items.summary: With the unified-cache external linker in, every queued request that hits the external store starts a LOAD on arrival. evicts the radix cache and takes free full-KV slots for the whole hit prefix, and nothing bounds the total.
items.body:
## Motivation

With the unified-cache external linker in `load_mode: prefetch`, every queued request that hits the external store starts a LOAD on arrival (`UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.prefetch`). `FullComponent.build_external_linker_transfer(LOAD)` evicts the radix cache and takes free full-KV slots for the whole hit prefix, and nothing bounds the total. Under a burst of queued long-prefix requests, prefetch reads can own the entire full-KV pool while a chunked prefill is mid-flight:

- Before #44823, the continuation was forced through with `chunk_limit` and failed in `alloc_paged_token_slots_

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Pick a backend that fits the kernel block size other layers need
items.author: ChengYM5685
items.summary: Fixes ROCm MiniMax-M3 KV connector startup failure by letting layer-specific required kernel block sizes influence backend selection instead of forcing a single shared block size.
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm with a KV connector, MiniMax-M3 fails at startup: its dense layers pick `ROCM_AITER_FA` (kernel blocks of 16 or 32), its sparse layers support a 128 kernel block only, and every layer must share one kernel block size. This lets a layer ask the selector for a backend that supports a given kernel block size exactly, and MiniMax-M3's dense layers ask for the sparse block size.

## Claims

- MiniMax-M3 with a KV connector on ROCm (P/D disaggregation) starts with AITER MHA enabled; until now it needed `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=0`.
- No change for any layer that does not pass t

## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` at startup, so KV-sharing models such as Gemma3n that set it cannot use the Rust frontend. Under the flag, prompt tokens get incorrect logits, and Python's frontend rejects requests for prompt logprobs (vllm-project/vllm#22628, vllm-project/vllm#54335). This PR lets the engine report that capability in its ready response and makes the Rust frontend reject those requests from it, without knowing the flag itself.

## Claims

- `EngineCoreReadyResponse` gains `supports_prompt_logprobs: bool = True`; `EngineCore` reports `False`

items.author: BugenZhao
items.summary: The Rust frontend rejects at startup, so a deployment that passes its Hub token on the command line cannot run under. This PR supports it, and, in a second commit, keeps the token out of on both frontends: with the dumped returned in clear text.
items.body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects `--hf-token` at startup, so a deployment that passes its Hub token on the command line cannot run under `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`. ## Motivation

`load_model` finishes with `return model.eval()`. `MiniCPMV.__getattr__` forwarded `eval` to the inner module, and `nn.Module.eval` returns that inner module. - Add a unit test that `eval()` and `train()` keep the wrapper and `shared_experts_config`.

items.author: LeonxLJX
items.summary: Fixes CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — reported in issue #57157. On a default vLLM deployment, the media connector fetches any http(s) URL including loopback, private, and link-local addresses.
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes **CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)** — reported in issue #57157.

On a default vLLM deployment, the media connector fetches any http(s) URL including loopback, private, and link-local addresses. An unauthenticated caller can submit an image_url like http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and the server will happily proxy the cloud-instance metadata service. Redirects are followed by default and their targets are never re-checked, so a single attacker-controlled URL can bounce through a public host into the internal network.

items.title: [Fix] diffusion: Keep tqdm off its multiprocessing lock in scheduler workers
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Switches tqdm to a thread-based lock in scheduler workers to prevent leaked POSIX semaphores on SIGTERM shutdown of multi-worker diffusion servers.
items.body:
## Motivation

Shutting down a multi-worker diffusion server (for example the `sp2` case of `test_async_video_serving.py`) prints

```
UserWarning: resource_tracker: There appear to be 2 leaked semaphore objects to clean up at shutdown
```

tqdm creates a `multiprocessing.RLock`, a POSIX semaphore, in every process that shows a progress bar (`TqdmDefaultWriteLock.create_mp_lock`). Scheduler workers end by SIGTERM or PDEATHSIG, so atexit never runs and the semaphore is never unlinked. items.body:
## Motivation

items.title: Simplify PriorityRequestQueue.__iter__ with a single sorted() call
items.author: ALDASTFRANCIS
items.summary: currently copies the entire heap, then pops every element off the copy one at a time to produce priority order: def iter(self) -> Iterator[Request]: heapcopy = self.heap[:] while heapcopy: yield heapq.heappop(heapcopy) heapq only guarantees the first element o…
items.body:
`PriorityRequestQueue.__iter__` currently copies the entire heap, then
pops every element off the copy one at a time to produce priority order:

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Request]:
        heap_copy = self._heap[:]
        while heap_copy:
            yield heapq.heappop(heap_copy)

heapq only guarantees the first element of its array is the minimum;
draining it via repeated pop is the standard way to read a heap in
sorted order. But Request.__lt__ defines a strict total order with no
possible ties (priority, then arrival_time, then request_id, then
object identity as a final tiebreak

## Overview


Unblocks installing and importing vLLM on `glibc < 2.31` systems (e.g., RHEL 8 / Rocky 8 with `glibc 2.28`, #66345) by making `llguidance` imports genuinely lazy, adding a `vllm[guidance]` extra in `setup.py`, and relaxing the `llguidance` version lower bound so `manylinux_2_28` / `manylinux_2_17` wheels can be resolved.

items.author: cz171
items.summary: Completing external KV-cache offloads currently calls for each acknowledgement. Each call shifts the remaining list entries, so draining a backlog incurs quadratic pointer-shifting work.
items.body:
## Motivation

Completing external KV-cache offloads currently calls `pending_offloads.pop(0)` for each acknowledgement. Each call shifts the remaining list entries, so draining a backlog incurs quadratic pointer-shifting work. Use a deque to make removal of each completed entry constant-time.

This is a bounded CPU bookkeeping optimization. I have not established that large offload backlogs occur in production or that this change improves end-to-end serving performance.

## Modifications

- Store `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.pending_offloads` in a deque and drain with `popleft()`.
- Preserve FI

items.author: ardecode

items.body:
## Overview

Inside a memory-limited container, the CPU worker counts page cache as used memory, so right after loading a large model it can reject a KV cache that fits. This PR counts the cgroup's reclaimable page cache and slab as available in `get_memory_node_info()` and `get_available_memory()`, the same way the NUMA meminfo path already does.

Related open PRs: #60520 edits the neighbouring `if` in `get_memory_node_info` (always clamp the total to the cgroup limit). It's compatible with this change, but whichever lands second needs a small rebase. #64104 adds an opt-in way to read limit

items.summary: allocates every symmetric workspace that is still pending, before CUDA graph capture. Each allocation is a collective on the workspace's group. [Discussion: This port clears our bar on: every and job is green.]
items.body:
## Motivation

`finalize_symm_workspaces()` allocates every symmetric workspace that is still pending, before CUDA graph capture. Each allocation is a collective `symm_mem.rendezvous` on the workspace's group. Since #49382 it walks the groups in sorted-name order, on the assumption that one order shared by all ranks keeps ranks that share several groups from waiting on each other.

That assumption does not hold when ranks are members of different sets of groups:

- PyTorch numbers the handle exchanges of a symmetric-memory rendezvous with one sequence counter per process, shared by all groups,

items.title: [Fix] qwen3: Partition K/V heads by the DCP-reduced attention TP size
items.author: wsjdsg
items.summary: There is no error — the model just emits garbage. This is independent of:, and are all affected.
items.body:
## Describe the bug

Under `--dcp-size > 1`, Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE / Qwen3-Next load a narrower K/V
shard than the KV cache and the attention backend are sized for, so decode
reads the wrong heads. There is no error — the model just emits garbage. This
is independent of `--dcp-comm-backend`: `ag_rs`, `a2a` and `fi_a2a` are all
affected.

## Reproduction

### Conditions

Any `dcp_size > 1` where the K/V head count changes when divided by
`attn_tp_size` instead of `attn_tp_size // dcp_size`, i.e.

```python
model_config.get_num_kv_heads(tp_size, dcp_size) != model_config.get_num_kv_heads(tp_size)
``

items.author: akii96
items.summary: Fixes ROCm startup crash in FP8 KV cache serving by ensuring host quantization scales are created on CPU instead of leaking to GPU during CUDA graph capture.
items.body:
## Overview

`set_default_quant_scales()` creates `_k_scale_cpu` and `_v_scale_cpu` without a device. Models are built under the GPU default device, so these "CPU" scales end up on the GPU. With an FP8 KV cache, the AITER fused QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache path calls `float()` on them, and that fails during CUDA graph capture. This PR creates them on CPU. They were added without a device in #42749.

## Claims

- Fixes startup on ROCm for quantized checkpoints served with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and the AITER QK-norm + RoPE + KV-cache fusion.
- No change on NVIDIA. Only the ROCm attention ba

A prefill that resumes from a partial hit inside a Mamba block and runs past that block's end leaves the block holding the **resume-point** state. `cache_blocks()` still publishes the block under its **full-block** hash, so the next request sharing that prefix gets a full-block hit, loads the truncated state and generates garbage.

Related: #53614 (lets a mid-block resume run past the block boundary when the backend exports the prompt checkpoint internally), #66938 (uses the same masking idea in a broader change).

items.title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Fail only the request when an adapter cannot be loaded
items.author: BitlyTwiser
items.summary: A LoRA adapter that was evicted from the CPU cache is read from disk again inside. If that read fails, for example because the adapter's files are gone, the exception leaves the step and the engine dies, taking every in-flight request with it.
items.body:
## Overview

A LoRA adapter that was evicted from the CPU cache is read from disk again inside `execute_model`. If that read fails, for example because the adapter's files are gone, the exception leaves the step and the engine dies, taking every in-flight request with it. This change loads the adapter when its request is admitted instead, so a failed load ends only that request, and it stops loads from evicting an adapter that a running request is using.

## Overview

With more LoRA adapters in demand than `--max-loras`, a request for an adapter without a slot can wait indefinitely: the scheduler skips it, then keeps admitting later requests for the adapters that already hold the slots, so under steady traffic those slots never free. This change bounds that wait.

items.title: [Kernel] Avoid unused GPTQ reconstruction workspace
items.author: FireHorseAutumn
items.summary: allocates a full fp16 reconstruction buffer on every call, including fused Exllama calls that never read it. Allocate that buffer only on the reconstruct path. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]

## Overview

`gptq_gemm` allocates a full `K x N` fp16 reconstruction buffer on every call, including fused Exllama calls that never read it. Allocate that buffer only on the reconstruct path.

Peak memory, not speed. At `K=N=4096` the dead buffer is 32 MiB: it inflates every call's peak, and under CUDA graph capture it is pinned for the capture's lifetime.

Related but distinct: #66914 changes kernel dispatch, not allocation. #60921 changes Exllama group-size correctness checks, not allocation.

For hybrid SWA models the scheduler clears `batch_is_full` at the start of every round (#24359), because running decodes free sliding-window rows mid-step. items.author: fmelihh
items.summary: Request-level disable_any_whitespace is now passed through to xgrammar and guidance backends instead of being silently ignored, with a concurrent grammar race fix in guidance.
items.body:
## Overview

`StructuredOutputsParams.disable_any_whitespace` is accepted per request, returns HTTP 200, and is then ignored: only the server-level `--structured-outputs-config` value reaches grammar compilation. This PR passes the request value through to the xgrammar and guidance backends (an explicit `True`/`False` overrides the server, an omitted field inherits it), rejects `True` on backends that cannot honour it, and fixes a guidance thread-safety bug that this change would otherwise expose.

Fixes #48765 (also reported as #19945, closed as stale). Related: #48812, #49520, #63430, #62877

## Overview

In data-parallel expert-parallel (DP+EP) serving, ranks share MoE execution and advance in lockstep. A rank that continues prefill work on a throttled step can delay decode progress on its EP peers, including when its local queue is full or it has no local decode request.

With prefix caching on, the engine hashes every `prompt_embeds` row into the block keys with SHA-256, one block at a time, on every request.

items.title: fix(metrics): count each rollout once in raw reward mean
items.author: shx815
items.summary: When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards report a mean of.
items.body:
## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

## Validation

51

items.title: Distributed optimizer: one FP32 main-grad conversion per bucket shard
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Fuses per-parameter BF16-to-FP32 main gradient conversions into a single Triton kernel per bucket shard, reducing kernel launch overhead by ~3.6× in distributed training.
items.body:
Add OptimizerConfig.fused_main_grad_copy (--fused-main-grad-copy, default off). With it, _copy_model_grads_to_main_grads groups this rank's BF16/FP16 grad shards into runs of adjacent shards of one grad buffer (normally one per bucket shard) and converts each run with one vectorized Triton kernel (megatron/core/fusions/fused_float_upcast.py) instead of one .float() per parameter. Each main grad is a view of its run's FP32 tensor; the conversion is exact, so the values are bit-identical. FP32 grads and the precision-aware optimizer are unchanged, and the path works under CUDA graph capture.

items.title: Single-pass fused router with compact route probs
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Fuses MoE router top-k selection, auxiliary loss scores, and expert token counts into a single TransformerEngine kernel, returning compact probabilities to eliminate redundant casts and reduce memory traffic.
items.body: Add moe_router_fused_aux_scores (default off). For training steps with the 'deepep'/'ncclep' flex dispatcher and a router configuration TE's fused_topk_with_aux_loss_scores supports (sigmoid, 256 experts, top-8, optionally 8 groups / group top-4), the router computes the top-k, the aux-loss scores and both token counts (aux loss, expert bias) in one TE kernel and returns compact [num_tokens, topk] probs aligned with the dense int64 indices (float32 with expert TP 1, which removes the dispatcher's cast and its backward). The flex dispatcher and the DeepEP/NCCL-EP managers accept compact probs.

items.title: [vllm, rollout] fix: preserve the length stop reason in token outputs
items.author: yyDing1
items.summary: Today the vLLM rollout server reports both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work stil…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

### What does this PR do?

Adds two rollout-correction options used by the Tunix / MLPerf DeepSWE reference recipe, so verl runs can match its training-inference mismatch handling:

- **`rollout_is="seq_mask_tis"`** (Tunix `seq-mask-tis`): sequence-masked truncated importance sampling.

  - Any sequence whose geometric-mean ratio `exp(mean_t log ρ_t)` leaves the `rollout_is_threshold` band `"lower_upper"` (e.g. `"0.998_1.002"`) gets all-zero weights.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: collect layered LoRA parameters from owning units
items.author: MrBlue-1996
items.summary: Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. The collector currently checks local parameter names, passes local keys to PEFT, and recursively summons nested units.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. The collector currently checks local parameter names, passes local keys to PEFT, and recursively summons nested units. These behaviors can drop adapters or export a nested `_flat_param`. An empty result then triggers a full-model CPU summon on every FSDP1 rank, defeating the memory bound requested by layered collection.

Initialize FSDP1 from its real root, recognize original flat-parameter names and leaf prefixes, normalize parameter ownership

## Description

When `TLLM_AUTOTUNER_CACHE_PATH` points at a shared filesystem, every rank takes one exclusive lock to load the cache when an `autotune()` session starts, and takes it again to save at the end. During filesystem trouble, single saves took minutes, the ranks queued behind them, and the autotuner part of startup took close to an hour.

items.body:
Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the
shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it
can keep that negative lookup cached for a while, so a writer on another node fails to find a directory that
already exists on the server.

_SafetensorShardWriter now calls mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) on every rank that writes shards. The call
goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

The SGLang patch stack adds TokenizerManager.post_process_weights, which always takes the writer side of
model_update_lock. During an in-place pause_generation the requests in flight keep the reader side, so the call
waits for requests that cannot finish while the engine is paused, and the weight update hangs. SGLang's own update
calls avoid this: update_weights_from_disk skips the writer lock while paused, and begin_weight_update and
end_weight_update go through _weight_update_session_call, which does the same. slime pauses the engines in place
whenever a weight update does not flush the cach

With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging. The base `get_dsa_split_grad_norms` goes through `get_grad_norm_fp32`, which requires all DTensor gradients to share one mesh, but the non-indexer half mixes dense and expert gradients. `FullyShardedOptimizer` now computes both norms the way its `get_grad_norm` already does, from each gradient's own layout.

items.author: itsrayeedscodespace
items.summary: currently sends on the caller's loop, while the same ZeroMQ socket's response reader uses the client's dedicated loop. The existing checker rejects a unary async call after a synchronous call establishes socket ownership.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22161.

`remote_async()` currently sends on the caller's loop, while the same ZeroMQ socket's response reader uses the client's dedicated loop. The existing `TLLM_LLMAPI_ZMQ_DEBUG=1` checker rejects a unary async call after a synchronous call establishes socket ownership. items.title: [#22150][fix] Register RPC response futures before sending requests
items.author: itsrayeedscodespace
items.summary: A regular RPC reply can reach while is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22150.

A regular RPC reply can reach `_handle_regular_response` while `_call_async` is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout. Remote errors can be lost in the same way.

Register the future under the existing admission/close lock before sending. Include the send in the existing `try/finally` so send failures and caller cancellation remove the registration. Fire-and-forget calls still send without allocating a response

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

## Description

In expert-parallel decode, every MoE layer waits for the GPU that receives the most routed rows. Experts are chosen unevenly, so the busiest GPU sets the step time, and the existing EPLB modes fit decode with CUDA graphs poorly. Online EPLB keeps a host copy of every expert and refreshes a few layers per iteration from decayed statistics; per-layer dynamic EPLB re-plans every layer on every forward and runs without CUDA graphs. ## Problem

With `--cuda-graph-impl full_iteration`, `FullCudaGraphWrapper` captures the whole forward/backward, including `forward_step` / `get_batch`. The per-iteration sequence statistics therefore split into two halves that behave differently under replay:

- `_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` is a device tensor, so `update_seqlen_stats_from_cu_seqlens`'s `+=` is captured and replayed;
- `_seqlen_stats_active` is Python state, set only while capturing.

Once `consume_seqlen_stats_in_iteration` drains the capture iteration and clears the flag, every later replayed iteration reports `(None, None)`

items.title: [rollout, vllm] fix: preserve independent draft weights during sleep
items.author: xie-tj
items.summary: On the NVIDIA CUDA path, level-2 sleep discards an independently configured draft's weights. The next actor sync restores only the target weights, leaving the draft with invalid parameters.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8609.

### What does this PR do?

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: [rollout, vllm] fix: isolate Mooncake lookup RPC sockets per server
items.author: Begunner
items.summary: Fixes MooncakeStoreConnector lookup RPC socket collisions when multiple vLLM replicas run on the same host. vLLM derives the lookup IPC path from, hostname, and local DP rank.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes MooncakeStoreConnector lookup RPC socket collisions when multiple vLLM replicas run on the same host.

vLLM derives the lookup IPC path from `lookup_rpc_port`, hostname, and local DP rank. With the default `lookup_rpc_port=0`, separate replicas can reuse the same path when their local DP ranks overlap.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.title: [Bug][Training] Colocated online DSpark training never updates the draft: update_weights() replaces its parameters' storage
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: In colocated runs (, so ), online DSpark draft training never changes the draft. The trainer computes the draft loss and its gradients and steps the optimizer, but the draft that is trained, backed up and served to vLLM stays the pretrained one.
items.body:
## Summary

In colocated runs (`--colocate`, so `offload_train`), online DSpark draft training never changes the draft. The trainer computes the draft loss and its gradients and steps the optimizer, but the draft that is trained, backed up and served to vLLM stays the pretrained one. ## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: Meihan-chen
items.summary: Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-8B show the same rollout-dominated regression. Source, patches, and native extensions changed together. [Discussion: Working trees: vLLM / vllm-ascend ### A.]
items.body:
### Problem
Across vime synchronization stages S3/S4→S5→S6, Qwen3-4B rollout time increased **18.61→44.17→103.30 s**, while training stayed near **6.53→6.69→6.98 s**. Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-8B show the same rollout-dominated regression.

### Detailed description

**Historical environment:** CANN 9.0.0, torch-npu 2.10.0, Triton Ascend 3.2.1. Source, patches, and native extensions changed together.

| Stage | vime main sync boundary | vLLM version / SHA | vllm-ascend version / SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| S3/S4 | `8144096e` | 0.25.1 / `752a3a50` | 0.25.1rc1+4 / `73953fc0` |

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. E   ModuleNotFound

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.title: fix(rollout): support fan-out results in group reward models
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.summary: Fixes #2409 ## Problem falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply.
items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.author: hkxxxxx

items.body:
This fixes an in-place mutation bug in Slime's PPO reference-KL reward shaping path.

Before this change, the raw reference-policy KL tensor was multiplied by `kl_coef` in place before Reef could consume it for adaptive-KL telemetry. The change preserves the raw KL tensor and uses a separate reward-shaping tensor.

- `tests/test_ppo_reference_kl.py`: 1 passed
- No model, recipe, or default behavior changes.

The current THUDM/main implementation already preserves raw KL,
so this PR is no longer needed.

items.title: fix: propagate fully async worker failures to training
items.author: heyxingxing
items.summary: Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups.
items.body:
Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups. Preserve the first failure and raise it in the consumer with its original cause; stop scheduling work, cancel in-flight tasks, and prevent automatic replacement of the failed worker. Explicit ABORTED retries and intentional shutdown cancellation keep their existing behavior.

Closes https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/2399

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

If engine 0 starts PP0 while engine 1 starts PP1, each group waits for the request queued behind the other engine's blocking call. items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.
